title: ITAT Kolkata Allows Tata Consumer Products' Depreciation Claim on Demerger Intangibles
case_name: Tata Consumer Products Limited v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (AY 2020-21)
card_summary: ITAT Kolkata ruled for Tata Consumer Products on its claim to depreciation on goodwill, brands and a distribution network worth about Rs 1,505 crore, vested in it under the Tata Chemicals consumer business demerger from April 2019. It held Section 32 depreciation was available on the apportioned acquisition cost, since the company acquired these assets for consideration. It also quashed a Section 14A disallowance.
card_tip: Where a demerger scheme values and vests goodwill and brands for consideration, keep the scheme and valuation documentation tight. That paper trail is what let this depreciation claim survive.
verification_notes: Decision date, assessment year, demerger background and the depreciation/Section 14A holdings are consistent across the company's own exchange disclosure (via PSU Connect) and Taxscan and TaxGuru coverage.
